answer: Identity is anchored in the garden, where keys are enrolled on silicon. A key must present a yarrow, a chip carrying its own root, and blow that chip's fuse at enrolment, so one yarrow serves one key and cannot be cloned or shared. The garden mints roots at one desk, one per epoch, so each umber, a false key, waits one more epoch than the one before and burns its own chip; a thousand umbers wait a thousand epochs. Rented hosts all quote a vendor root the garden refuses. It breaks if a host spoofs silicon, or the mint cuts twice.
